vocab.title: Match each expression to its meaning
defs: the salary plus the benefits: the full amount the company pays
a number that is close, but not exact
the minimum and the maximum salary for a position
compared with the same period in the year before
the level of a position, which decides its salary range
the place in the budget where the money for a position is planned

paras: A requisition tells a story, but the committee reads it through numbers. The first number most managers write is the salary. It is important, but it is only part of the cost. Benefits, such as health insurance, a meal allowance and the yearly bonus, usually add up to twenty-five to thirty-five percent of the salary. The number the committee wants is the total cost: salary plus benefits, per year and per month.

The second check is the pay grade. Every position sits in a grade, and every grade has a salary range, with a minimum and a maximum. An offer near the top of the range is possible, but it needs a reason. An offer above the range is a different conversation, because it changes the grade, and often the budget.

Then comes the budget line. A position that is already on a budget line, such as a replacement, is easier to approve. A new position needs new money, and the HRBP has to show where it comes from. Comparisons help here: if payroll is up eight percent year over year and the business is up twelve, the request tells a different story from a request in a business that is not growing.

Finally, precision has its moment. In the first conversation with a manager, a ballpark figure is enough: roughly seventy thousand a year. In the document for the committee, the numbers must be exact, they must add up, and the dates must be clear. A total that does not add up is the fastest way to lose the committee's trust.

items.situation: The manager asks: "How much does the new controller cost?"
tips: With benefits, the total cost comes to roughly sixty-nine thousand dollars a year.
total cost, not only the salary.

items.situation: She asks if the offer is inside the range.
tips: Yes. Fifty-three thousand is just under the top of the range.
just under = a little less than.

items.situation: She wants a number now, before you check the details.
tips: A ballpark figure is seventy thousand. I'll send the exact number tomorrow.

items.situation: She asks if payroll grew this year.
tips: Yes, payroll is up eight percent year over year.

items.situation: She asks which grade the position is.
tips: It is pay grade seven. The range is forty-two to fifty-five thousand.

items.situation: She asks if the two salaries fit the budget line.
tips: Let me work it out. I think they add up to just under the budget line.
work out = calculate; add up to = the total.

listenings.text: Hello everyone. Before the committee meets on March thirteenth, a quick reminder about the numbers on every requisition. Please don't send me only the salary. I need the total cost. In our companies, benefits add up to roughly thirty percent of the salary, so a salary of fifty thousand dollars comes to about sixty-five thousand a year. Second, check the pay grade and the salary range. If the offer is above the range, tell me before the committee, not after. Third, the budget line: every position must sit on a budget line. And one more number. Our headcount cost is up fifteen percent year over year. Fifteen, not fifty, but the committee watches it closely. A ballpark figure is fine for the first conversation. For the committee, I need the exact numbers. Thank you.

Hi Camila, it's Rafael, from the rental company, about the backfill for the fleet controller. I have the numbers now. The position is grade seven, and the salary range for grade seven is forty-two to fifty-five thousand dollars a year. The candidate we like asks for fifty-three thousand, so that is just under the top of the range. With benefits, the total cost comes to roughly sixty-nine thousand a year, or just under five thousand eight hundred a month. The start date is May fourth, and the controller's last day is May twentieth, so we pay two people for just over two weeks. Can you check if that still adds up to less than the budget line? Thanks, talk soon.
